# System Overview and Architecture

AlphaProject RAG ChatBot is a production-grade, local-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) web application. The system answers user questions strictly grounded in uploaded private documents with inline numbered citations such as [1] and [2]. When retrieved evidence is insufficient in strict document mode (`strict_documents`), the assistant abstains rather than hallucinating unsupported claims.

The backend stack uses Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Alembic database migrations, and Celery distributed workers backed by Redis 7. The frontend stack uses Next.js 15 and React 19 with a dark-mode workspace interface, Server-Sent Events (SSE) token streaming, and NextAuth JWT session management.

# Document Ingestion and Structure-Aware Chunking

The ingestion pipeline supports five document formats: PDF (`.pdf`), Microsoft Word (`.docx`), Plain Text (`.txt`), Markdown (`.md`), and HTML (`.html`). Uploaded files are validated against a maximum file size limit of 50MB and deduplicated per owner using a SHA-256 content hash (`content_hash`).

Documents are parsed into structure-aware semantic blocks that preserve real section headings (`section_path`), heading levels (`heading_level`), page boundaries (`page_number`), and semantic block types (`block_type` such as `method`, `results`, `procedure`, `requirements`, `acknowledgement`, and `references`). The `ChunkingEngine` splits semantic blocks using recursive character splitting measured in `cl100k_base` tokens with a default `chunk_size` of 512 tokens and `chunk_overlap` of 51 tokens (10% overlap). Administrators and users can customize `chunk_size` (64 to 4096 tokens) and `chunk_overlap` (0 to 1024 tokens) during upload or re-indexing.

# Vector Database and Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline

PostgreSQL 16 with the `pgvector` extension stores document chunks in the `document_chunks` table. Each chunk stores a 1024-dimensional dense vector in the `embedding` column (`Vector(1024)`) indexed with an HNSW cosine similarity index (`ix_chunks_embedding_hnsw`, `m = 16`, `ef_construction = 200`). Full-text lexical search uses a PostgreSQL `TSVECTOR` column named `search_vector` indexed with a GIN index (`ix_chunks_search_vector_gin`) and maintained automatically via the `trg_chunks_search_vector` trigger and explicit SQL `to_tsvector('simple', content)` population.

Local embeddings are generated by Ollama using the `mxbai-embed-large` model, which outputs 1024-dimensional dense vectors. During retrieval, the system executes both vector cosine similarity search and BM25-style lexical full-text search (`ts_rank_cd` with `to_tsquery('simple', ...)`), then merges the candidate lists using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with constant `k = 60`. Near-duplicate chunks with cosine similarity above `0.95` are deduplicated, boilerplate sections (such as acknowledgements and table of contents) are demoted by section policy, and the top-20 candidates are reranked into the top-5 evidence clusters.

# Intent Detection and Grounded Generation

The `RetrievalIntentService` classifies each user query into one of seven intents: `definition`, `factual`, `summary`, `compare`, `extract`, `multi_hop`, or `question`. Questions starting with "what is", "how does", or "how do" are classified as `definition` queries with a confidence threshold of `0.30` and single-section support allowed. Multi-section evidence is only required when the query intent requires synthesis across sections and the target document actually contains at least two distinct sections.

Local text generation runs on Ollama with the `qwen2.5:7b` large language model. Because loading `qwen2.5:7b` (4.7GB) on CPU can take longer than 30 seconds on the first request, the backend performs an automatic model warmup during startup and enforces a `120`-second first-token timeout (`FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120`) and a `60`-second inter-chunk stream timeout. Chat responses support two modes: `strict_documents` (Document only, abstaining when support is low) and `hybrid_general` (Allow outside knowledge, explicitly badged in the UI when outside knowledge is used).

# Security, RBAC, Rate Limiting, and Operations

Authentication uses JWT access and refresh tokens with bcrypt password hashing. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) supports three core roles: `admin` (full system, user, evaluation, and document management), `editor` (upload and manage documents), and `viewer` (chat and view owned documents). API rate limiting enforces sliding-window limits of 30 requests per minute for `/api/v1/chat`, 10 requests per minute for `/api/v1/documents/upload`, and 100 requests per minute for general endpoints.

The `/health` endpoint verifies connectivity and readiness across four components: PostgreSQL (`pgvector`), Redis (`PING`), Ollama (`mxbai-embed-large` and `qwen2.5:7b` model presence and warmup state), and the Celery worker (`ingestion.process_document` task registration). Every chat request emits a `STRUCTURED_CHAT_LOG` JSON entry recording query intent, candidate counts, top-k scores, BM25 contribution, step-by-step latency (`rewrite_ms`, `retrieval_ms`, `rerank_ms`, `generation_ms`, `total_ms`), token usage, and abstention status.
